title: Halcyon AI - Goldset Contract & Load Agreement
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet + pricing by 2025-10-03
Customer to provide 500 golden prompts and 200 regression cases by 2025-10-06
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run in staging (week of 2025-10-13)
SE to provision temporary VPC peering details for test run by 2025-10-07
action_items: Jordan Lee - Share benchmark spreadsheet and draft pilot SOW - due 2025-10-03
Ravi Patel - Upload sample payloads, 500 golden prompts, 200 regression items to shared S3 - due 2025-10-06
Priya Natarajan - Prepare test plan and estimator for GPU hours + concurrency - due 2025-10-05
Ben Walker - Confirm network egress and KMS policy for staging - due 2025-10-07
summary: POC scoping to lock down acceptance criteria and lift baseline workload for a 3-week pilot. Agreed deliverables: customer provides goldset + regression suite, Redwood runs benchmark in staging with latency/cost/accuracy metrics, and both teams align on pass/fail gates and timelines.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. quick roll call?
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: Sofia here, CTO.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Ravi, Head of ML.
[00:15] Aileen Cho: Aileen product.
[00:17] Ben Walker: Ben infra.
[00:20] Priya Natarajan: Priya from Redwood, SE.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Great, goal for today is to agree success metrics, size the workload for the POC, and define the goldset/regression plan.
[00:35] Sofia Martinez: High level we want to validate three things: quality parity with our current model, latency under 350ms p50 for single-turn prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under target that we'll finalize after price sheet.
[00:50] Ravi Patel: For quality, we care about hallucination rate on knowledge-heavy prompts and strict format adherence for our JSON responses.
[00:58] Priya Natarajan: Noted. When you say hallucination rate, are you thinking binary presence/absence or graded severity?
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Probably graded. critical hallucinations (factual contradiction) vs soft hallucination (missing detail). We'll want thresholds: critical < 1% and soft < 10% across the goldset.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Good, we'll map scoring to those bands. For format validation we can run deterministic checks: JSON schema conformance, field-level regex, and token-length truncation checks.
[01:30] Aileen Cho: Also need deterministic routing — if Redwood falls back to smaller model we need to flag those outputs as lower confidence.
[01:38] Priya Natarajan: We'll surface model variant and confidence metadata in the logs so you can filter.
[01:44] Ben Walker: On infra, we will run this in your staging VPC via peering if possible. security questions: KMS for keys, retention for logs, SOC2 attestation.
[01:55] Jordan Lee: We'll share our security pack after call. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for Private/Dedicated pilots.
[02:05] Sofia Martinez: Timeline wise we want a 3-week POC: week 0 instrument, week 1 load/functional smoke, week 2 quality/bench. Can you run a single big benchmark in week 2?
[02:15] Priya Natarajan: Yes. We recommend a staged run: small proof (100 prompts) -> full goldset (500 prompts) -> sustained load ramp for concurrency. How many QPS do you target?
[02:26] Ravi Patel: Typical peak for prod is 80 qps but the feature expects bursty traffic; for the pilot let's validate up to 40 qps sustained and a burst test to 120 qps for 30s.
[02:38] Priya Natarajan: Good; that will let us size batching and estimate GPU-hours. We'll return a pre-run estimator.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: On metrics we propose capturing p50/p90/p99 latency, avg tokens per call, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rates, format-fail % and semantic-accuracy % (human graded subset).
[02:58] Ravi Patel: Semantic accuracy — we need rubrics. will you do automatic pass/fail and a small human audit?
[03:05] Priya Natarajan: Yes. Automatic checks for strict items (format, hallucination detection heuristics), plus a 10% human audit of the goldset outputs for edge-case scoring.
[03:15] Ben Walker: Regarding data, will you store KV cache or logs? we need retention controls.
[03:20] Marcus Chen: We can enable ephemeral KV cache for the pilot and set logs retention to 30 days, and redact PII before retention.
[03:30] Aileen Cho: On golden prompts — we will hand over 500 prompts representative of our top-2 product flows. They include multi-turn context and optional system instructions. Expect some noisy items though.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: That's fine, we'll annotate and run a cleaning pass. For regression tests, we need negative cases: prompt injections, malformed JSON, and adversarial hallucination prompts. How many regression tests do you have?
[03:54] Ravi Patel: At least 200 to start. Should cover format edge cases and adversarial.
[04:00] Priya Natarajan: Ok so target artifacts from customer: 500 gold prompts, 200 regression items, a small sample of production traffic for token-distribution, and your acceptance checklist. We'll produce: benchmark plan, runbook, cost estimate, and scoring rubric.
[04:15] Sofia Martinez: On scoring rubric we want weighted metrics: 40% semantic accuracy, 25% hallucination severity, 15% latency, 10% format adherence, 10% cost. If the weighted score >= 82 we pass.
[04:29] Jordan Lee: We'll mirror that scoring but propose a soft-fail policy for latency (if latency slightly over but accuracy good we flag but still pass conditionally).
[04:38] Aileen Cho: Can Redwood annotate outputs with hallucination severity automatically?
[04:42] Priya Natarajan: We can run heuristics: citation-mismatch rules, entity hallucination detectors, and a confidence score. It's not perfect but will catch the majority.
[04:52] Ben Walker: For the load test env, we need the estimated egress and a list of IPs to whitelist.
[04:57] Marcus Chen: We'll provide IP ranges and the staging subnet for the run. Also recommend a short-maintenance window for the benchmark to avoid background noise.
[05:06] Ravi Patel: Cost sensitivity — for the pilot it's fine, but if cost looks 3x our target we'll need to test quantized variants.
[05:13] Priya Natarajan: We can include a quantized model run as an alternate path and compare quality/cost tradeoffs.
[05:20] Sofia Martinez: How will rollbacks work if we see regression mid-pilot?
[05:24] Jordan Lee: We'll keep snapshot versions and can rollback to the previous model variant or route a % of traffic to a fallback. Also will set auto-fallback triggers if hallucination rate exceeds a threshold.
[05:35] Aileen Cho: Data residency — pilot data stays in staging region us-west-2.
[05:38] Ben Walker: Fine. Also provide a simple postmortem template for any failures.
[05:43] Jordan Lee: We'll include that in the runbook.
[05:46] Priya Natarajan: To recap next steps: Redwood sends security pack + benchmark spreadsheet + draft SOW; Halcyon shares goldset + regression; schedule bench window.
[05:57] Ravi Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[06:00] Jordan Lee: None. We'll prepare the estimator and send it out.
[06:04] Sofia Martinez: Ok thanks all.
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
